62: Sustaining: saṃyatam = yad asmān saṃyacchati, that which supports us
Amśu may also be interpreted as metal-streaks in an ore block (Kalyan)
Having wise designs: kavikratuḥ = krāntaprajñaḥ krāntakarmo vā, possessing wisdom or possessing sacred rites; Kaviḥ = kāntaḥ (cf. RV 9.064.30)
Seven ceremonies: The back are the three oblations, the benches are the three vedas , and the ceremonies are the seven hymns, chāndas
I.e. as a hero resolutely stands among the enemy's cattle, so the Soma resolutely stands among the sacrifices
Have for us: i.e., grant us
I.e. these worlds honour you; the rivers observe your bidding
63: Making all our acts prosperous: i.e. making Soma propitious for the sake of our rites
Tyā harito daśa : haritaḥ = horses or rays of the sun
The summit of the ground: i.e., the raised plural ce, the plural ce of divine sacrifice
64: The firmament: samudram may mean the vasatīvarī waters
Yat = yadā; thus, 'when the horse of burden neighṣ.., then you who are the horse of burden of the sacrifice are plural ced in the vasatīvarī waters
I.e., he does not approach the sacrifice of those who do not worship; he only approaches the sacrifice of worshippers
Sapient speech: vipaścitam = prajñayā pavitrām, cleaning (?) by wisdom
To the battle: metaphorically, for sacrifice
Sūryaḥ is separated from dṛśe and explained as suvīryaḥ ; Ṛdhak = pṛthak , also used to mean 'prospering' ( Nirukta 4.25)
65: Well-armed: or, having fine sacrificial implements, such as sphya, kapāla
Or, I urge you to grant us food
By these flexible fingers: ayā = from i, to go; ayā vipā anayā = itastato gacchandibhir etābhir madīyābhir aṅgulibhiḥ
Śaryaṇāvat = possessing sweet juice; reference to a lake in the western part of Kurukṣetra region
Ṛṣayo vai sarasvatyām satramāsata: Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 2.19; five castes: niṣādas are added to make the number five
The dispensers of food: Soma grants all the boons in the hope of which the worshipper offers the Soma to the gods
66: Those two halves: dhāmanī = pūrvādipakṣau, the first and second fortnights of the lunar month, the sides or halves of the month resembling in their increase and decrease the sides of a creeper, whose leaves alternate; or, nāmāni aṃśusomātmake, the two names ( aṃśu and Soma); 'on earth under the name aṃśu by granting the desires of all mankind (Soma rules) this world; in heaven by giving the gods your lunar digits you are the winner of their affections. The gods drink the digits of the (moon) Soma by means of their growth and diminution one by one (i.e., as the moon waxes and wanes); dhāmanī probably means the two abodes (or stations) of the Soma
I.e. Soma whose attributes are the seasons such as spring, exists wherever day and night spread; because day and night are dependent on the Soma (i.e., the moon)
Pṛṣṭha = the lower part of heaven, i.e., the earth
Seven kindred priests: Or, the seven kindred rivers urge you with thei rfingers, i.e., send you forth to be cleansed by the vasatīvarī and ekadhanā waters
In the quickly-made filter: Or, in the filter which overcomes guilt
I.e., our fingers desire the Soma juices in order to cleanse them again and again
To the ocean: the wooden vessel in which the Soma is collected
Five orders: four varṇas and the niṣāda ; or, the gandharvas , pitṛs , gods, asuras , and rākṣasas ; or, the gods, mankind, gandharvas, apsarasas , serpents and pitṛs
Continually goes to the gods: atyaḥ = devān santatam gantā bhavati
I.e. then the priests by means of the Soma, perform Indra's praise
67: Heroic: i.e., the instrumental gator of everybody's good actions (sacrifice)
In all his paths: Or, in this sacrifice; Yāman = yajña because it is reached, i.e., obtained by the gods
Who wears a beautiful tiara: kapardine = kalyāṇa mukuṭavate; this also means, having hair braided like a cowrie shell ( kaparda )
Genitive rator of the praises of the wise: Or, in the midst of the wise, it is you who does genitive rate speech
Or, utter a sound; Vāyum = śabdam
Divine body: divine, because it increases, viz., sons; the light is the light of the sun, lightning
Yajus . 19.43; your three...forms: i.e., fire, wind and sun
Worshippers: Or, the troop of gods, Indra and others
The battle-axe: paraśuḥ = chedakaḥ pavamānaḥ , as if Soma were metaphorically called a battle-axe and implored to turn his edge against foes only (tam eva śatrum nāśayatu)
Mātariśvan = Va+yu, because it breathes in the atmosphere, antarikṣe śvasiti; the food is sweetened and purified by the purifying wind and the man eats it
Here follows a khila of 19 verses in praise of pavamāna hymns
68: His station: i.e., the uttara vedī , the northern altar; it protects the head: śiraḥ = śīrṇam bhūtajātam (the withered world?)

This may refer to the fact that rain is caused by the sun, with which Soma is identified; the last part of the verse may refer to the sun, which appears in the daytime, and the moon, which appears at night
The falcon brought from far: a bird in the form of gāyatrī brought it from heaven
69: The fosterer: ūdhani = Indra, because he is the nourisher of everything
Diffuseṣ..arrow: santaniḥ: as an adjective with somaḥ , i.e. diffused in the ladles; as a noun, the arrow discharged (by the foe)

His spouse: i.e., the herbs, naptiḥ = naptṛh, i.e. the fourth genitive ration. Prajāpati begets the gods; the gods beget the rain; the rain begets the herbs; Or, it means the offspring of Soma; Soma nourishes the herbs with his rays. Soma 'separates' the herbs at the lip to make them fruitful ( Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 2.1.3); ṛtam yāte = yajñam gacchate, i.e., yajamānāya

The first part of the verse praises Soma; Soma at the time of entering the wooden vessels makes a noise; the cows, the propitiating hymns of praise, gather round him; the hymns of praise approach the god's station.
Shining vestment: i.e., the milk; Āditya's brilliance: nabhasmayam = ādityamayam ādityasya svabhūtam tejas

By the sprinklers: Or, praised by the priests who give the Soma; On our return: niveśe = svagṛham prati praveśane nirgamane vā, on our entering our home or leavin git; dvipade, catuṣpade are datives from -pad
You, Soma are...: Soma is treated as a plural ral by attraction; or, as the plural rality of the pitṛs is applied to Soma

To battle: sātim: an epithet of Indra, sarvaiḥ sambhajanīyam; also, meaning 'battle, from so, to kill; casting off infirmity: casting off infirmity that pervades all their limbs, becoming youthful; vavr. from vṛ, that which covers the body; Haritaḥ = becoming the horses that bear the Sun
70: Thrice seven kine: may signify the 12 months, the 5 seasons, the 3 worlds and the sun; the four waters are the vasatīvarī waters and the three ekadhana ) waters ( Taittirīya saṃhitā 5.4.12.2)
Opens: i.e., fills them with water

Both classes of beings: the movable and stationary or animate and inanimate creation; or, men and gods; 'the Soma fertilizes the plural nts at the sacrifice, and streams of men flow forth', the plural nts being part of the stationary ( sthāvara ) creation, and men belonging to the movable ( jaṅgama )
Among the midmost mothers: mātṛṣu; Madhyamāsu = plural ced in the atmosphere; look after both races: gods and men, i.e., 'men by granting them their desires, gods by bestowing oblations upon them'
Asuras: śurudhaḥ = śucā rundhanti parān, they avert painfrom others; Śaryāha = haananasādhanair iṣubirhantā vīraḥ ; in RV. 67.16.39, śarya = an enemy; Śarya = an arrow, paṇaiḥ śatrūṇām hantā
His green-tinted horns: i.e., the streams of the Soma juice
Sinless: Or, motionless, i.e., plural ced the vessel; the three ingredients: tridhātu, three ores; or, water, curds, and milk
He who knows the country: 'as by telling him he protects (helps) him, so do you who know the roads of the sacrifice protect us by telling us the sacrificial paths'
Bear us safe acrss: i.e., across dangers or evil spirits, duritānyatīya pāraya
71: The all-sustaining water of the Sun: Or, taking nabhaḥ as accusative ative, and payaḥ as genitive tive, 'the firmament the supporter of the water'; the mighty Sun: Brahma is explained as 'the mighty uplifted one that destroys darkness, or the supreme sun; parivṛḍham, as if deriving brahma from vṛṃh or bṛṃh
Asura-slaying tint: i.e., green;or varṇam means 'protecting strength'; the food: i.e., the Soma; Pituḥ = juice or food; Tanā = in the filter outstretched by the sheep-skin
Or, at the sacrifice which nourishes the gods by bestowing oblations on them
The clouds: Or,mountains; Inwhom: Indra is here regarded as soma pavamāna ; Varimabhiḥ = urutvair mahattvaiḥ
His ray: varṇa = from vṛ, keeping off, beating back; 'his ray repelling his foes'
Flying gracefully: suparṇaḥ = a hawk; supatanaḥ, going gracefully, because it is carried off by gāyatrī in the shape of a hawk
72: Indra's belly: i.e., the droṇakalaśa; with their ten united fingers: sanilabhiḥ = liṭ, having one nest ( nida ); Sanīḷa = samānasthāna, samānanivāsa
The daughter of the sun: i.e., the dawn, beacause, at that time the noise of the effusion of the Soma is great; the praiser: vinaṃgṛsaḥ = kamanīyam stotram gṛhṇātīti; arm
For strength: Or, for the sake of food; Enemies: matiḥ = abhimānān śatrūn
The plural ce of birth of the sacrifice: i.e., the northern altar
The shaker of the libation: ādhūnvate = making the ādhāvana (shaking) with the three filaments of the Soma , after the adābhya libation
73: On the jaw of the sacrifice: srave = the plural nk of the Soma press, adhiṣavaṇa phalaka , which is the jaw of the sacrifice; the ships: i.e., the four pots for the āditya , āgrayaṇa , ukthya and dhruva libations.

The voice of the firmament: vācam = voice of the firmament (or middle world) residing in the Soma; 'Soma stand in the firmament; the King Soma sit among the gandharvas '' (somo vai rājā gandharveṣvāsīt) ( Aitareya Brāhmaṇa ). The voice of the firmament is thunder, and the rays of the Soma refer to the moon or the Soma juices identified with the rain

His rays: spaśaḥ = sārabhūtā raśmayaḥ; or, spies; never shut their eyes: 'but always keep watch to know the evil and the good, or always keep on alert as kings to guard against enemies; fixed each in his plural ce: 'in every plural ce there are barriers strewn with snares (to keep off and catch the wicked or the rākṣasas ), or, prisons filled with fetters
The blind and deaf: i.e., spiritually blind and deaf, those who do not see good objects-- those who do not hear the praise of the gods
Their servants: spaśaḥ = vācā vaśinaḥ (obedient voices)
He plural ces in his heart: i.e., combines in himself; the three purifiers are agni , vāyu and the sun

Varuṇa's tongue: i.e., the vasatīvarī waters, which are on the tip of Varuṇa's tongue; the wise...reached it: 'it' refers to the tip of Varuṇa's tongue; the wise reach it by their praises or oblations.
74: Brilliant: or, swift as a horse; that nourish the kine: payovṛdhā, that feeds the milk of kine and the sap of herbs
The prop of the earth: cf. RV. 9.089.06; may he unite: yakṣat = saṃyojayatu; Āvṛta = by its own unaided strength
Whose road is hither: i.e., to this our sacrifice
The bond: nābhiḥ = binding; from naḥ, to bind
He sprinkles: i.e., distils into the vessels
The four digits: nābhaḥ = rays, dīptayaḥ; or, digits ( kalaḥ ) of the Soma; derived from nābhas , heaven and the root naḥ, to bind (nābhaḥ = nabhaso bādhikaḥ, obstructing heaven)

Successfully reaches: sasavān = saṃbhajan, enjoying, possessing; who has seen a hundred winters: śatahimāya = bahugamanāya, i.e. one who attains many things; elsewhere, śatahimāya = aparimita- kālā , lasting for an endless time
75: Speaking: i.e., resounding, or replying to the praises of the worshippers; a third name unknown to his parents: a name not given at birth at the called cnāmakaraṇa; rocane divaḥ = dyulokasyā dīpyamāne somebhiṣū yamāṇe satī ; somayājin is an instrumental nce of a third name ( Baudhāyana )
The milk of the sacrifice: 'the priests milk the stones as calves (milk the cows)' ( Taittirīya Saṃhitā 6.2.11.4).
Loud-sounding: āhanasas = having slaughter, or having utterance; or, being struck or pressed; or, having praises
76: Witht he rite: i.e., at the very time the rite is being performed
77: More beautiful: vapuṣo vapuṣṭaraḥ = sowing seed more than any other sower of seed
He detaches: saḥ = Soma; a reference to the hawk, who is afraid of Kṛśānu, the protector of Soma. The legend is in Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.26
Milk-giving: urubja = from uru+ap+jan, producing abundant water (milk)

The maker of all, clever in work, the juice, mighty unassailable Varuṇa flows from heaven for the sake of him who go hither and thither; the friend of the adorable (Soma) is effused in affliction uttering a sound like an ardent horse amidst a herd (of mares). [
78: Many are the paths for you to follow: or, 'there are ancient paths for you to go to Indra, and a thousand bay horses standing in the cups'].
In the midst: in the middle of the sacrifice, i.e., in the cups
79: The stones devour you upon the cowhide: Soma was poured out upon a black antelope's skin; but,t he Soma was measured on a cowhide for the purpose of selling
80: Whom the kine praise: aghnyaḥ = āhananīha gāvaḥ , the kine which are brought to the sacrifice and milked for the curds with which the Soma is mixed, are lowing
For his food: or, for the sake of getting food for the sacriricer
81: Aśnoti is a predicate of yat; somaḥ as the subject of aśnoti: 'he acquires what is in the world above and what is in this world; 'he acquires from the next world what is there and from this world what is here'
Our riches: no gayam, i.e., asmabhyām pradeyam dhanam, the wealth to be bestowed on us
May the genitive rous (gods) meet together to us-- Pūṣan, Pavamāna, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Vāyu, the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭā, savitā, and beautiful Sarasvatī. [
82: Parjanya: i.e., the rain; somaḥ is implied in mahiṣasya parṇinaḥ and is the subject of dadhe. The mountains are the grinding-stones; the navel of the earth is the oblation. svasaraḥ = fingers
Pajra: i.e., the earth; Soma is its offspring, because it is produced in the ground
83: The lord of cattle: nidhāpatiḥ (the lord of snares) = nidhipatiḥ (the lord of treasure)
In the liquid water: haviḥ in contrast to nabhaḥ ; to the battle: i.e., the sacrifice
84: Call: when the gods hear the Soma flow, they come to the sacrifice; call the celestial people: or, speak to the godly folk, i.e. me, the ṛṣi, saying: sādhu saṃbhakta

Goes round about: i.e., protects; Indu accompanies the sacrifice (sacrificer), connecting it (him) with the gods (the desired end--phalaiḥ), separating it (him) from the asuras (calamities), as the sun for the protection (of sentient beings) accompanies the dawn, connecting it with light and separating it from darkness
The people of heaven: daivyam is considered with indram, 'the lord of the gods'
I.e., aindrasya hārdi, in such a way that Indra's heart is friendly
85: In the heaven: nāke = free from pain, the plural ce called havirdhāna ; Divaḥ = dyotamānasya yajñasya
I.e., mātarā = nirmātryau; i.e., the two mother; or, the two parents (pitarau)
86: For Indra's strength: dhāyase = dhārakāya; or, 'to Indra's supporting', i.e. to support Indra
Through your functions: 'by the supporting streams of juice'

Navel of the earth: yajñamāhu bhuvanasya nābhim: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.4.18.2; associate with the wave of the waters: to indicate the effect of the Soma in producing rain by combining in the clouds with the solar rays
Wearing a coat of mail: i.e., clothed in light
Through whom: ataḥ = yasmāt somāt ( tṛpta indraḥ ); 'since his (Soma's) station is in the highest heaven, therefore he (Soma) triumphs'
To the heavenly abodes: i.e., the bellies of the gods
Or, you did open the mountain-side which concealed the cattled stolen by the Paṇis
The seven kine: the seven verses, gāyatrī and others, or the seven rivers; to the plural ce of sacrifice: or to the water; ṛtam is added: ṛtam yoniḥ = ṛtasya yoniḥ, meaning water
Hundred-streamed: or, śatadhāraiḥ = Soma and juices; Harim : a reference to Indra ; Abhiśriyaḥ = mixed with milk; Udanyuvaḥ = desiring (Indra's rain)
The seven sister mothers: i.e., the seven rivers clothe the Soma with their water
The two men: i.e., the praiser and the worshipper; or, secular and sacred people (laukikavaidikau)

Smear and grease and anoint: añjate, vyañjate and samañjate are synonyms; into the seething torrent: sindhor ucchvāse = liṭ, in the hreathing of the river; i.e., going to an elevated plural ce, the receptacle of the juice, rasasyādhārabhūte ucchrite deśe gacchantam
The measure of days: beacause, the rule as to the length of day depends on the increase and decrease of the moon's digits, Soma being here regarded as the moon
Triple beverage: tridhātu = three vessle, the droṇakalaśa, āhavanīya and putabhṛt; or, just, three metallic ores: gold, silver, lead/coopper
May we offer ample praises: bṛhad vadema = liṭ, may we say much (or speak loudly); or, may we solicit much wealth
87: In RV. 9.005.02, the ṛṣi is Uṣanas, son of Kavi , or Uṣanas the poetical
88: After this: i.e., after harnessing of the wagon. ūrdhvā = asmād virodhād unmukhāni; Svarṣātā = locative of svarṣāti, 'that which is fitted for the attainment of heaven, i.e., battle
The divine blameless folk: i.e., the Maruts: maruto vai devānām viśaḥ ( Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2.2.5.7)
Varuṇa: 'I quickly perform the sacrifices of you the cover'; Varuṇa = varāka
89: The father milks him: pitā (pālako lokāḥ) = Adhvaryu , who extracts the juice of the Soma which is born from the heaven as from a father; or, the first milk may be the yajamāna and the second the adhvaryu; or duhe may be repeated as a mark of respect
90: Advances: prayacchati, bestows; Soma is the genitive rator of earth by giving rain, and of heaven by obtaining the oblation
91: On whom the minds of the gods are fixed: tasmin hi teṣām manāṃsyotāni ( Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 2.10)
Adorable: viśvavāra, who is worthy to be chosen by all
Diffuse the luminaries widely: uru = urūṇi related to jyotiṃṣi
92: The seven wise ṛṣis: Bharadvāja , Kaśyapa , Gotama , Atri , Viśvāmitra , Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha
Accompanied by all the gods: or, having all-pervading light
93: The wives of the sun: jaḥ = jayaḥ ; the quarters of the horizon are called the sun's wives because they are made manifest by the light of the sun
As the infant by its mother: the infant longs for its mother and is sustained by her milk; Sandadhanve = has flowed with
Nourish the cow's udder: the Soma entering the herbs, etc., nourishes the cow who eats them
Your capacious mind: purandhi = tvadīyā bahuvidhā dhīḥ
94: Vie with each: spardhanti = aham purastācchodhayām yaham puraḥ śodhayāmītyahamahamikayopatiṣṭhanti
The abode of the ambrosia: i.e., the firmament, the home of the waters; call upon Indu like kine lowing: svasare = of the laudations on the day of sacrifice; of the kine towards their stall
95: The green-tinted Soma being let loose propels the voice that indicates the path of truth as the boatman (propels his) boat; the bright Soma reveals to his worshipper on the sacred grass the secret names of the god. [
The priests milk forth: grāvaṇo vatsā ṛtvijo duhanti ( Taittirīya Saṃhitā : 6.2.11.4); who dwells in three abodes: or, tritaḥ may be an epithet of somaḥ ; varuṇam may be an epithet of indram
Set free the understanding: i.e., make his (?Indra's) mind favourably disposed to grant wealth
96: Hastily made: rabhasāni = indrasya vegenāgame nimittāni,?caused by Indra's hasty arrival
The Brahmā of the gods: i.e., the king of the gods; or, it may mean the brāhmaṇa of the priests; the ṛṣi: yaḥ parokṣam paśyati sa ṛṣiḥ, ṛsirdarśanāt ( Nirukta 2.11)
Yourself unharmed: avataḥ = tair, i.e. śatrubhir abhigataḥ
Desirous of the mixture: or, with a noise
Wise with wisdom: there is a plural y on the word, kavi ; separating gībhiḥ from kaviḥ , the explanation is: he passes through the filter with praise
I.e. the region of the moon which is above that of the sun
Like a richy decorated man: maryo na śubhraḥ ; the plural nks: the ladles; the soma has already been effused and filtered
97: Sound aloud: dhanvā = imperative of dhanv
The praiser: devaḥ = Soma ; as a wild boar makes a noise with its foot: varāhaḥ = effused on a good ( vara ) day ( ahan )-- epithet of Soma; Pada = padāni, abodes, i.e., the filters
Walking like swans: haṃsāsaḥ = wounded by the enemy; Amāt = śatrūṇām balāt trāsitāḥ santaḥ ; another interpretation: the vṛṣagaṇas have gone from hence to their home
The Soma appears green-tinted by day: Soma is not visible in the daylight; Ṛjra = straight going, ṛju-gāmī, i.e., clearly visible, vispaṣṭaḥ = red or brown

Giving health to our home: śaṃgayīm = sakhasya nivāsabhūtam, inhabiting happiness; the kinsmen: because Indra and the winds are in the relation of praised and praiser; imān vāyūn = us approaching you, asmān tvām abhigacchataḥ
For the support he affords: dharmaṇi = the reason ( nimitta ) of the praise; i.e. the duty of acquisition and preservation (or the duty of securing property), yogakṣema viṣayam karma
Soma is twofold: i.e., abides among both gods and men
Endeavouring to gain the favour of the gods: āyajyavaḥ sumatim viśvavārāḥ
Look down from heaven: avacakṣi, an imperative
The bearer of the oblation: i.e., the worshipper; the three texts are: ṛk, yajus . and sāman ; Brahmaṇaḥ = the spureme, parivṛḍhasya Soma; the kine come to Soma to mix their milk with him
With great noise: Sāmaveda has madena for raveṇa
Stock the cattle from the rock: us. = muṣ; i.e. 'stole (ransacked) the rock with regard to (i.e., for) the cattle'
Threefold protection: it protects against cold and rain
Flow quickly into the cups: camvoḥ = adhiśavṇa phalakayoḥ; apsu is related with parisrava
Advance to the brown water: māṃścatva = manyamānānām cātake, 'scaring away (?) those who are respectful'; Badhraḥ = the illuminator of all or the root of all--the sun

In a fight on horseback: māṃścatve = a horse, i.e., a battle fought with horses; derived from: makṣu carati ; Pṛśane = bāhuyuddhe, an arm-fight (person nal combat); Unbelievers: acitaḥ = those who do not make an agnicayanam (preparation of the sacred fire-plural ce), i.e., infidels
Three outstretched filters: the three are the fire, wind and sun; the one is the woollen filter
98: To the woollen filter: druṇā = hiyānaḥ (tena pūryamāṇaḥ); Hitaḥ = sent forth on all sides; or, praised by the worshippers
To every man: śāśvate = numerous as being possesssed of children
99: In RV. 9.006.003, the ṛṣis are the two rebhasunus = son of Rebha. spread out the white filter: nirṇijam vayanti = they weave a garment
Approaching: gāvaḥ ; 'which the cows take up in their mouths, eating it in the form of grass
The wise worshippers instrumental uct: śāsate = they desire him
100: The vast firmament: śravaḥ = śravanīyam, i.e. antarikṣam
101: I.e., prevent the dogs or rākṣasas from lapping the Soma
They bestow food upon us: samasvaran = liṭ, they sounded food for us
Let no mortal: 'No death-giving, i.e., rite-obstructing dog'; Arādhasam = stingy, rādhakakarmarahitam
102: With the seven supports of the sacrifice: i.e., with the seven metres; or, deriving sapta from. sṛp, they effuse the Soma with the vasatīvarī water
I.e., yojanāni which may also mean, roads or stages; in RV.1.018.05, yojanā = a means for inducing the gods to yoke their horses, i.e., a hymn
The seven mothers instrumental uct the (Soma) the instrumental tutor (of the sacrifice) when born for the prosperity (of the worshippers) to that this firm Soma is cognizant of riches. [
Dīdhitim is deried from dhṛ, the supporter of the rite
103: I.e. the droṇakalaśa (wooden cask), āhavanīya (that into which the Soma may run), and pūtabhṛt (holding the filtered Soma)
Purified by priests: vāghat = carried by the priests;or, fetching wealth for the worshippers
105: Sāma veda reads dhāraya for ddīdharam
106: This effused soma...filtered for Indra: 'this munificent effused Soma is filtered for Indra's sutenance; indrāya bharāya is like a gerund
Conquering the Vṛtra in the waters: 'Conquering the Vṛtra for the sake of the waters'; or, conquering ahi in the firmament
With their fingers: dhībhiḥ = dhītibiḥ; or, by their praises
107: Into the pitcher: anupe = on the bank; or, in a watery low-lying plural ce, nimne deśe
In a shining robe: i.e., the filter
Vas and true: ṛtam bṛhat relates to the Soma, atyantam satyabhūtaḥ
Purified in the cups: camu = camuṣu; effused on the plural nks
Sāmaveda has tavāham for utāham; duhanaḥ for sakhyāya; far beyond the sun: paraḥ is an adjective for sūryam; Sūryam = soma, may we fly to you, the distant sun
108: Interpretation: Who by his might cut the quick-moving waters of the firmament from out of the cloud, you get a herd of cattle and horses
Into the cups: adhiśavana phalakāyaḥ, in the plural nks of the press
He has assumed his shining robe: he has blended himself with the milk, for the sake of being cleansed
109: Extolling the gods: prajām is separated from urāṇaḥ ; Urāṇaḥ = uru kurvāṇaḥ, i.e. devān bahu kurvāṇaḥ
Prerayam = stimulating (Indra); Tośate = hanyate, is beaten, abhiṣūyate, is effused
110: Streaming forth: saniṣyadat = sambhajan, distributing (blessings?): from san, to acquire
The chief of men: or, the men of old
Holy: ṛtavā = yajñavān, having a sacrifice
111: With the rays yoked to it: svayugvabhiḥ refers to suraḥ ; the repetition adds dignity; with the ṛkvans, with the seven-mouthed ṛkvans: rikvabhiḥ = stutimadbhiḥ; second ṛkvans = tejobhiḥ; thus, 'with encomiastic splendours' is the rendering; the seven-mouths are for taking up the Soma juice
By the mothers: the vasatīvarī waters
You are invincible: you two, i.e., Soma and Indra; or, better, so that you two, you and Vajra
112: The singeṛ..papa...mamma: kāruḥ = maker of praises; 'maker', 'poet'; tataḥ and nānā mean father (dada) and mother; or son and daughter respectively
Easy to draw: auspicious; Upamantriṇaḥ = narmasacivāḥ, boon companions
113: Śaraṇyāvat: a lake in the Kurukṣetra region
Ārjikā; the country of the ṛjikās
Daughter of Sūrya: śraddhā vai sūryasya duhitā ( Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 12.7.3.11)
Engendering delight: someṇānandam janayan, 'producing joy with the Soma';
Where wishes: 'where the desired gods and the inevitably solicited Indra and other gods exist
The wishes of the wisher: the desired god
